job.title: Director Enterprise Systems and Services
job.description:
Hybrid Details: Onsite Tue-Wed

Position Overview:
  • Seeking a polished, strategic enterprise technology leader to guide experienced technical managers and lead transformation across a large, complex, and rapidly growing academic healthcare environment.
  • The environment supports approximately 35,000 people and 4,000 servers across clinical, research, administrative, and business operations.
  • This is not a hands-on engineering role.
  • Four senior managers report to this position and provide the technical depth.
  • The director must be technically fluent, but the primary focus is strategic leadership, executive communication, relationship-building, business judgment, and organizational transformation.
  • The most important skill is the ability to build relationships and communicate effectively with C-suite leaders, peer directors, enterprise architects, Epic and application leaders, clinical and research stakeholders, vendors, and business partners.
  • The ideal candidate brings independent judgment, offers a distinct perspective, and can respectfully challenge assumptions while helping shape enterprise technology strategy.
  • The focus is transformation, modernization, and continuous improvement.

The manager is seeking someone who can help:
  • Keep pace with continued organizational growth
  • Modernize and transform the technology environment
  • Evaluate and advance cloud and AI opportunities
  • Ensure the technology organization is structured effectively
  • Make strategic platform and infrastructure investments
  • Balance clinical stability with research innovation
  • Support a complex institution with competing lines of business
  • Improve enterprise reliability, scalability, and operational performance

Requirements:
  • Director-level leadership experience in enterprise infrastructure, enterprise systems, platform services, or technology operations
  • Experience leading large and complex organizations (UTSW has 4000 servers and 35k employees & growing)
  • Experience supporting a large-scale environment, ideally comparable to approximately 35,000 people and 4,000 servers
  • Experience managing senior managers or multiple technical teams
  • Strong executive presence and C-suite communication
  • Experience leading technology transformation, modernization, or organizational growth
  • Strong business acumen and financial judgment
  • Experience balancing competing operational, clinical, research, and business priorities
  • Experience with cloud, AI, infrastructure modernization, or technology lifecycle planning
  • The ability to lead technical teams without personally performing day-to-day engineering work
  • Experience in healthcare, academic healthcare, financial services, or another highly regulated and mission-critical environment
  • Healthcare or academic medical center experience is strongly preferred, although financial services and other reliability-sensitive industries may be transferable.

Selling Points
  • The opportunity to lead technology strategy at a nationally recognized academic medical and research institution
  • A stable organization with significant growth and long-term technology investment
  • Meaningful executive visibility and partnership across the institution
  • The opportunity to lead transformation involving cloud, AI, infrastructure modernization, and enterprise systems
  • Direct impact on patient care, clinical operations, research, education, and administration
  • A complex and mission-driven environment where the work has tangible importance
  • Access to the TRS pension, employer retirement contributions, and employee-only medical coverage at no monthly premium beginning day one.

Job Summary
  • The Director of Enterprise Systems and Services Service Delivery and Project Portfolio provides strategic and operational leadership for enterprise technology services within a complex, highly regulated, mid-to-large organization operating in a 24/7 environment.
  • This role oversees service delivery, incident management, project portfolio governance, enterprise architecture, budgeting, capital planning, and technology infrastructure initiatives. The director ensures reliable, secure, and scalable solutions aligned with organizational objectives.
  • The director collaborates with business leaders to drive innovation, improve operational performance, establish technology standards and policies, and lead continuous improvement through root-cause analysis and service optimization.

Required Education and Experience
  • Bachelor’s degree in a related field
  • Ten years of progressively responsible related experience
  • At least three years in a supervisory capacity
  • Experience with ITIL, including the ability to develop operational sustainability plans and related tasks to accomplish organizational objectives

Preferred Qualifications
  • Current or former technical industry-related certifications
  • Experience in healthcare, academic healthcare, financial services, or another highly regulated environment
  • Experience leading enterprise infrastructure, platforms, systems, or technology operations
  • Experience managing critical production environments
  • Experience with service delivery, project portfolio governance, capital planning, and enterprise architecture

Primary Responsibilities
  • Direct and oversee day-to-day service deliverables and impacts within the Enterprise Systems and Services division
  • Review ServiceNow incidents to ensure timely resolution and appropriate prioritization and escalation
  • Partner with division leadership and ESS management to manage operational priorities
  • Assist with strategic and operational project portfolio planning
  • Ensure approved projects are executed and implemented as planned
  • Direct enterprise architects in delivering sound, well-vetted enterprise solutions
  • Manage infrastructure and computing asset lifecycle strategies
  • Assist with forecasting and budgeting for aging and end-of-life technology
  • Support resource planning for projects and initiatives across IT divisions and business partners
  • Participate in annual capital planning
  • Identify innovative solutions that improve the efficiency of Information Resources services
  • Establish policies and procedures for server hardware, operating systems, storage, compute, and related components
  • Partner with the scientific and technical community to evaluate future technology trends
  • Consult with business partners, application analysts, vendors, and other stakeholders on project demand and planning
  • Evaluate design and build requirements, hardware and software specifications, pricing, and ongoing operational needs
  • Represent the division in root-cause analysis activities
  • Identify process and procedural improvements that increase the reliability of centrally managed technology
  • Perform other duties as assigned

job.title: Business Analyst – Application Design, Redesign & Modernization
job.description:
Hybrid Details: Greater Boston Area, MA - Onsite/Remote
Duration: 8 months to start 

Project Summary:
The client Information Technology Team supporting the Department of Developmental Services (DDS) within the is seeking to contract a highly motivated Business Analyst – Application Design, Redesign & Modernization with experience documenting existing workflows and Business and functional requirements related to Human Services Management and/or Healthcare applications.  DDS supports individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities including autism spectrum disorder, to enhance opportunities to become fully engaged members of their community.

Position Overview:
  • The Business Analyst – Application Design, Redesign & Modernization will be integral to large projects for applications that support operations, investigation and incident management, quality management, and legal business units for DDS as well as business processes related to these core functions.
  • Under the direction of a Project Manager/Business Analyst (PM/BA), the Business Analyst will be involved in the modernization of applications including Home and Community Services Information System (HCSIS) and Quality Enhancement License and Certification (QE5).
  • HCSIS is the primary application for DDS to monitor Center for Medicaid Services (CMS) services.  These services include the individuals served under the four Acquired Brain Injury / Moving Forward Plan (ABI/MFP) residential and nonresidential waiver programs administered by MassHealth/CMS.
  • QE5 is the application DDS uses to monitor CMS provider qualification assurances.
  • The successful candidate must have substantial hands-on experience leading the functional design or redesign of complex enterprise applications.
  • The candidate will assess existing applications and workflows, identify functional gaps and system dependencies, define future-state application behavior, and translate business policies, regulations, operational needs, and user requirements into detailed, implementable functional designs.
  • This position requires more than requirements documentation or meeting facilitation experience.
  • The Business Analyst – Application Design, Redesign & Modernization will actively shape application solutions and independently own business analysis and functional design deliverables. 
  • Experience with case management, healthcare, human services, public-sector, or other highly regulated applications is strongly preferred.  

Detailed List of Job Duties and Responsibilities:
  • Lead discovery, current state assessment, requirements elicitation, workflow redesign, and functional solution design activities involving business users, provider representatives, technical teams, and project leadership.
  • Analyze and, when necessary, reverse engineer existing application functionality, workflows, business rules, user roles, data flows, integrations, reports, controls, exceptions, workarounds, and system dependencies.
  • Identify functional gaps, conflicting requirements, redundant processes, usability issues, manual workarounds, regulatory constraints, and opportunities to simplify or improve application behavior.
  • Design future state application workflows and functional behavior, including user roles and permissions, task routing, approvals, reassignment, validations, notifications, escalations, exception handling, auditability, reporting, and operational controls.
  • Develop detailed business and functional analysis artifacts such as current state and future state process models, use cases, user stories, functional specifications, business rule catalogs, role and permission matrices, screen and field requirements, data definitions, interface requirements, reporting requirements, acceptance criteria, and requirements traceability matrices.
  • Evaluate functional design alternatives and clearly document recommendations, tradeoffs, dependencies, assumptions, constraints, and impacts on users, operations, data, integrations, reporting, etc.
  • Lead functional design reviews and walkthroughs, resolve requirements and design gaps, obtain stakeholder decisions and approvals, and maintain traceability from business need through design, development, testing, and implementation.
  • Proactively identify scope changes, design conflicts, delivery risks, unresolved decisions, dependencies, and potential impacts, and escalate them to project leadership with recommended actions.
  • Communicate complex business, functional, and technical concepts clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.

Preferred Qualifications:  
  • Minimum five (5) years of progressively responsible Business Analyst experience on complex application-development, redesign, or modernization projects, including at least three (3) years directly responsible for functional application design or redesign.
  • Demonstrated recent experience independently owning major business analysis and functional design deliverables.
  • Demonstrated experience assessing an existing or legacy application, defining future-state functionality, evaluating design alternatives, and supporting the selected design through development, testing, and implementation.
  • Experience participating in at least two substantial application implementations, redesigns, replacements, or modernization efforts across multiple phases of the software-development life cycle.
  • Experience translating complex policies, regulations, operational procedures, and business rules into implementable application behavior and testable requirements.
  • Experience leading discovery, requirements, workflow design, and solution design sessions with business stakeholders, subject matter experts, and multidisciplinary technical teams.
  • Demonstrated ability to create high-quality functional-design artifacts such as process models, use cases, user stories, functional specifications, business rules, screen and field requirements,  acceptance criteria, and requirements traceability matrices.
  • Strong understanding of the full software-development life cycle and practical experience working in Agile, hybrid, or iterative delivery environments.
  • Ability to identify conflicting requirements, challenge assumptions constructively, evaluate functional alternatives, recommend solutions, and drive issues to resolution.
  • Ability to work independently, manage multiple analysis and design priorities, and deliver complete, internally consistent work products with limited supervision.

job.title: Senior HIM Specialist
job.description:
Hybrid Details: Onsite initially with potential for hybrid flexibility following training 
Duration: 3 to 6 months to start

Position Overview
We are seeking an experienced Senior HIM Specialist with a strong background in Enterprise Master Patient Index (EMPI), patient identity, and data integrity to support a healthcare organization in Dallas, TX. This position is responsible for maintaining the accuracy and integrity of patient information across the electronic medical record. The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience researching and resolving complex patient identity issues, including duplicate records, overlays, demographic corrections, deceased-patient updates, and patient portal/proxy access.

Because changes made within the EMPI can impact appointments, patient portal access, medical records, and other downstream systems, this position requires exceptional attention to detail and the ability to thoroughly research information before making changes.

Key Responsibilities
  • Research, identify, and resolve duplicate patient records and overlays
  • Review, verify, and correct patient demographic information, including names and dates of birth
  • Process deceased-patient updates after reviewing and validating available documentation
  • Perform patient record merges, corrections, flags, and other data-integrity updates
  • Review and process MyChart proxy/access requests involving minors, parents, guardians, adoptive parents, and incapacitated adults
  • Validate appropriate supporting documentation before granting or modifying patient access
  • Utilize Epic, Care Everywhere, and other available healthcare systems to research patient information
  • Review multiple sources of information to ensure changes are accurate before updating the medical record
  • Monitor and respond to patient identity/data-integrity requests received through phone and departmental mailboxes
  • Maintain the privacy, confidentiality, accuracy, and security of protected health information
  • Meet established productivity, quality, and turnaround-time expectations
  • Collaborate with HIM leadership and team members to resolve complex patient-record issues

Required Qualifications
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • 2+ years of healthcare experience with a related vocational certificate or degree OR 3+ years of healthcare, business, and/or HIM experience in lieu of a certificate
  • Previous experience working within Health Information Management, EMPI, patient identity, or healthcare data integrity
  • Strong knowledge of electronic medical records and patient demographic information
  • Excellent attention to detail and critical-thinking skills
  • Ability to independently research complex issues and make accurate, well-supported decisions
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills

Highly Preferred Experience
  • Candidates with direct hands-on experience in the following areas are strongly preferred:
  • Enterprise Master Patient Index (EMPI/MPI)
  • Epic
  • Duplicate medical record resolution
  • Patient record overlays
  • Patient record merges
  • Demographic corrections
  • Deceased-patient workflows
  • MyChart proxy/access requests
  • Epic Care Everywhere
  • HIM data integrity or patient identity management
  • RHIT or other related HIM credentials are a plus but are not required.

job.title: System of Care Evaluator, Research Data Analyst
job.description:
Hybrid Details: in-person meetings can occur at the office and\or in community settings within Rhode Island
Duration: 4 years to start 

Position Summary
The client is building a more coordinated, accessible, and effective behavioral health System of Care. The System of Care Evaluator, Research Data Analyst will collaborate with the SOC Project Director, DPI administrator, Co-Qualitative Evaluators, Executive Leadership, state agency partner and community partners.

This role will include support of evaluation design and methodology, monitoring evaluation plan implementation, monitoring data collection, recommending any midcourse corrections, merging data from various data sources, engaging in data quality checks, conducting data analysis and developing regular data reports with data visualization for various audiences.

What You Bring to This Work
This role is for someone who believes public systems can work better for children and families, and who wants to be part of making that happen from the inside. You'll thrive here if you:
  • Keep children, youth, and families at the center. You see the family behind every policy, contract, and data point, and you hold System of Care values (family-driven, youth-guided, community-based, trauma-informed, and culturally responsive) as working principles.
  • Think in systems. You understand that children's behavioral health spans many agencies, funding streams, and providers, and you look for how the pieces connect rather than working in silos.
  • Treat relationships as infrastructure. You know that trust with providers, partner agencies, and families is what makes change stick, and you invest in it consistently.
  • Are comfortable building while moving. Much of this work is new or evolving. You can bring structure to ambiguity, make progress without a perfect roadmap, and adjust as you learn.
  • Balance urgency with patience. You bring energy and follow-through, and you also understand how government works and can navigate process without losing momentum.
  • Lead with curiosity and humility. You value the expertise of people with lived experience and frontline providers as much as your own, and you're open to having your assumptions challenged.

Key Responsibilities
Support of the Evaluation Plan and Methodology
  • Guide the evaluation plan and methodology with understanding of various evaluation plan designs and methodologies
  • Guide the Logic Model within the overall evaluation plan
  • Ensure the evaluation plan is consistent with the SOC grant purpose and aims
  • Monitor the fidelity to the evaluation design and methodology
  • Ongoing monitoring of the evaluation plan implementation
  • Make mid-course recommendations where necessary
Outcomes and Metrics
  • Co-develop and refine the Evaluation\ Logic Model Outcomes
  • Co-develop objective, measurable, realistic, attainable, outcomes consistent with the SOC aims
  • Co-develop outcomes ranging from process to impact and complementary to the qualitative outcomes
Data Collection and Monitoring
  • Co-develop a data collection process and protocol based on the evaluation plan design and the State’s SOC infrastructure
  • Engage and educate data analysts within the client, State Agencies and community providers who are data contributors to the SOC evaluation on the data collection methodology and protocol
  • Monitor the data collection process for timeliness, accuracy, validity, and reliability
  • Provide any ongoing data collection support to the SOC grant
Data Management and Data Analysis
  • Conduct data merging and data management of the various data sources
  • Conduct data quality checks and provide feedback where issues arise
  • Conduct data analysis from descriptive statistics to advanced statistics with various data types (i.e. categorical data, continuous data etc.)
  • Conduct data analysis primarily in SAS
Data Reporting
  • Develop regular and ongoing data reports for various audiences
  • Develop data reports with various formats such as data briefs, and\or quarterly reports and\or annual reports
  • Develop data reports to communicate the data inclusive of and not limited to various graphical, tabular, data visualization representation based on the nature of the data and audience
  • Develop reports consistent with the SOC grant funder
Cross-Sector and Interagency Alignment
  • Represent the client in interagency initiatives with State agency and community-based partners and organizations.
  • Facilitate and participate in workgroups and advisory bodies that include providers, families, youth, and community stakeholders.

Required Qualifications
  • Master's degree in a research data analytic field - Public Health, Social Sciences
  • [3+] years of progressively responsible experience in designing and conducting research, program evaluation, data merging, data quality, data analysis and reporting
  • Demonstrated experience supporting and leading implementation of grants, contracts, and strategic planning initiatives.
  • Ability to manage multiple complex initiatives at once with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to travel within Rhode Island for meetings and site visits.

Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience with federal grants, especially SAMHSA or other HHS awards.
  • Knowledge of children's behavioral health, the System of Care framework, and child welfare.
  • Experience engaging in research, data analysis in the areas of children’s behavioral health
  • Experience in or with state government, or with Medicaid-funded services.
  • Experience engaging families and youth with lived experience in policy and program design.

job.description:

Position Overview:
  • The client is looking for a highly skilled and experienced candidate to fill the Cloud Engineer position within the Enterprise Data Management & Engineering (EDME) department.
  • This role focuses on leading and advancing Mass Health Data Modernization initiatives such as SENDPRO, Enterprise Data Catalog, Data processing Pipeline optimization and automation by leveraging AWS Cloud, Snowflake and other data services.
  • Key responsibilities include Supporting SENDPRO and Data Modernization initiatives.
  • The ideal candidate will collaborate across various teams, including data management, engineering, business analysis, quality assurance, and analytics.
  • The goal is to enhance the efficiency, scalability, and overall performance of our cloud data platform.
  • The client is the agency responsible for administering the Medicaid and Children’s Health Insurance Program (collectively known as MassHealth). MassHealth offers health coverage services to eligible members, including families, individuals with disabilities, children, long-term unemployed adults, and seniors, through various programs, including fee-for-service and managed care.
  • The ideal candidate is an expert in Administration and support of Data Services.
  • You can clearly articulate and implement different data ingestion patterns depending on the use case.

job.title: ERP Support Specialist
job.description:
Hybrid Details: On-site 3 days/week

Job Description:
The Enterprise Support Specialist II provides Tier 2 support for enterprise information systems that support the organization’s operations, including Oracle Fusion, Oracle Cloud WMS, and related platforms. This role is responsible for troubleshooting system issues, supporting integrations, and maintaining application performance and reliability.
The Specialist collaborates with Database Engineers, developers, vendors, and business users to support system functionality, enhancements, and upgrades. This role also leads patching cycles, regression testing, and change management processes while serving as a mentor to Tier 1 support staff and contributing to continuous improvement initiatives.

JOB DUTIES:
Core Competencies
  • Strong knowledge of enterprise applications (Oracle Fusion ERP/SCM/HCM or similar platforms)
  • Technical proficiency in SQL, REST APIs, and system integrations
  • Analytical thinking and problem-solving skills
  • Understanding of business processes and system alignment
  • Effective written and verbal communication across technical and non-technical audiences
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills
  • Collaboration and cross-functional teamwork
  • Mentorship and knowledge sharing capabilities
  • Commitment to continuous improvement and operational excellence

Essential Responsibilities
Enterprise Application Support
  • Provide Tier 2 support for enterprise systems, including troubleshooting, issue resolution, and escalation.
  • Monitor system performance and ensure operational reliability.
  • Support system functionality across Oracle Fusion, WMS, and related platforms.

System Integration & Development Support
  • Support and maintain system integrations, APIs, and data flows.
  • Collaborate with Database Engineers and developers on enhancements and fixes.
  • Assist with reporting, data analysis, and system optimization efforts.

Change Management & Release Support
  • Lead change management, version control, and release processes.
  • Coordinate quarterly patching cycles, including regression testing.
  • Lead QA/UAT testing efforts and manage promotion of updates to production.

Continuous Improvement & Optimization
  • Evaluate and recommend system enhancements and configurations.
  • Identify opportunities to improve system utilization and business processes.
  • Collaborate with users to drive adoption and operational efficiency.

Documentation & Training
  • Develop and maintain system documentation, SOPs, and training materials.
  • Provide mentorship and support to Tier 1 IS staff and end users.
  • Facilitate knowledge transfer and user training sessions.

Vendor & Stakeholder Coordination
  • Coordinate with vendors (e.g., Oracle) and support partners to resolve complex issues.
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders to prioritize and manage system needs.

Operational Support
  • Manage multiple support requests, projects, and operational tasks simultaneously.
  • Participate in after-hours on-call rotation as required.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned.

EDUCATION:
Required
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Information Systems, Information Technology, Computer Science, or related field

Experience
  • 3–5 years of experience supporting enterprise applications
  • OR
  • 5–7 years of experience supporting enterprise applications in lieu of degree

Preferred
  • Experience in healthcare or supply chain environments
  • Experience with Oracle or Microsoft SQL

job.title: IT Strategic Sourcing & Purchasing Consultant
job.description:
Hybrid Details: Springfield, MA - Hybrid

Duration: 2 months to start (with potential for extension)

Job Description
  • The IT Strategic Sourcing & Purchasing Consultant will provide procurement support across the organization, with primary responsibility for IT-related sourcing, supplier management, contract negotiations, and renewal optimization.
  • In addition to supporting technology procurement activities, this role will assist with sourcing and purchasing initiatives across other spend categories as business needs require.
  • This consultant will partner closely with IT, Purchasing, Finance, Legal, and business stakeholders to drive value through strategic sourcing, effective supplier management, and efficient procurement operations.
  • The role will also be responsible for performing day-to-day purchasing functions, including requisition processing, purchase order management, contract amendments, and procurement administration.
  • The ideal candidate is a hands-on procurement professional with strong negotiation skills, exceptional attention to detail, and the ability to build productive stakeholder relationships while achieving cost savings and process improvements.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Sourcing
  • Serve as a procurement partner for IT-related spend categories, including software, SaaS, hardware, cloud services, telecommunications, and professional services.
  • Support sourcing activities across additional indirect and direct spend categories as needed.
  • Lead and support RFIs, RFQs, RFPs, supplier evaluations, and competitive bidding events.
  • Negotiate pricing, contract terms, statements of work, and renewals to achieve optimal commercial outcomes.
  • Identify opportunities to consolidate suppliers, contracts, and renewals across the organization to leverage purchasing volume and improve pricing.
  • Conduct spend analysis, market research, and supplier benchmarking to support sourcing decisions.
  • Partner with stakeholders to develop sourcing strategies that balance cost, quality, service, and business requirements.
  • Support supplier performance management and relationship development.
Purchasing Operations
  • Create, review, and process purchase requisitions and purchase orders in accordance with company policies and procedures.
  • Manage purchase order revisions, change orders, amendments, and closeout activities.
  • Facilitate contract renewals and amendments while ensuring compliance with procurement requirements.
  • Maintain accurate procurement records, pricing information, contracts, and supplier documentation.
  • Coordinate with Accounts Payable, Legal, Finance, and suppliers to resolve purchasing, invoicing, and contract-related issues.
  • Monitor open purchase orders and ensure timely follow-up and completion.
  • Support procurement reporting, spend analysis, savings tracking, and supplier metrics.
Required Skills & Qualifications
  • 5+ years of procurement, purchasing, and strategic sourcing experience, with a strong preference for technology-related products and services, including software, SaaS, hardware, cloud services, and professional services.
  • Demonstrated negotiation and supplier management expertise, with a proven ability to secure favorable pricing, contract terms, and measurable cost savings.
  • Experience reviewing, negotiating, and managing contracts, renewals, amendments, and supplier agreements, while identifying opportunities for spend consolidation, supplier rationalization, and procurement optimization.
  • Strong relationship-building and communication skills, with the ability to effectively partner with IT and business stakeholders while balancing operational needs, risk, and cost objectives.
  • Highly analytical, detail-oriented, and organized, with strong problem-solving skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities, sourcing initiatives, and procurement transactions simultaneously.
  • Proficiency with ERP and procurement systems, Microsoft Excel, and Microsoft Office applications, including experience supporting purchasing operations such as requisitions, purchase orders, and spend analysis.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Knowledge of software licensing models, SaaS agreements, cloud services, and IT supplier ecosystems.
  • Experience supporting procurement transformation or centralization initiatives.
  • Familiarity with supplier relationship management and procurement best practices.

job.title: Senior Project Manager
job.description:
Duration: 12 months to start 

Job Description:
To work with agencies and/or organizations to strengthen cross-system collaboration and implement integrated business solutions within an integrated system; to be responsible for several project developments simultaneously; to perform planning, coordination, stakeholder communication, risk management and monitoring/reporting functions throughout the software development life cycle (SDLC); and to do related work as required.

Supervision Received:
Works under the general direction of an agency program lead or a consortium with considerable latitude for the exercise of initiative and independent judgement; assignments are subject to review for results obtained in adherence to established policies and procedures.

Illustrative Examples of Work Performed:
  • To work with State agencies and/or organizations to strengthen cross-system collaboration and implement integrated business solutions within an integrated system.
  • To be responsible for special project development authorized and delegated by an agency program lead.
  • To perform research and analysis on various issues affecting stakeholders of health and human service programs and solutions.
  • To serve in a highly responsible communications capacity representing a number of stakeholders in their contact with vendors and business partners.
  • To perform complex program analysis and evaluation of departmental services.
  • To resolve issues and to prepare reports on complex issues for consideration and decision by the agency business and program leads.
  • To be responsible for developing and maintaining a continuous coordinated effort in liaison with vendors and business partners.
  • To keep agency program leads informed of decisions and recommendations on system, programs, and policy issues.
  • To make frequent contact with business subject matter experts relative to decisions and recommendations on system, program, and policy issues.
  • To do related work as required.

Required Skills:
  • A thorough knowledge of the principles, practices and techniques of project management related to developing interdepartmental programs and services within complex system applications;
  • A thorough knowledge of the planning, requirement analysis, design, development, testing, deployment, and maintenance phases of the SDLC and the ability to apply them within a large-scale integrated health and human service system
  • The ability to research and prepare reports, process flows, business requirements and recommendations for dissemination
  • A thorough knowledge of, and the ability to, evaluate the operational and system impact of stakeholders and to understand their demands and needs for information about the department's programs and objectives
  • The ability to communicate effectively with a variety of stakeholders
  • Related capacities and abilities.

Education and Experience:
  • Education: Such as may have been gained through possession of a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Public Administration, Business Administration or a related field.
  • Experience: Such as may have been gained through considerable employment in a highly responsible position involving responsibility for the planning, coordination, stakeholder communication, risk management and monitoring/reporting functions throughout the software development life cycle.
  • Or any combination of education and experience that shall be substantially equivalent to the above education and experience.
